Which trackers and which workspace shapes must the Cockpit handle in v0.1.0, and which are left for later?

To decide:

- **Trackers.** GitHub through `gh`, local markdown under `.scratch/`, GitLab through `glab`, and "Other" trackers described in prose (the seed proposes an agentic collect step for those).
- **Workspace shapes.** A single repo, a multi-root workspace, and a workspace folder that is not the repo root.
- **Several maps.** A repo with more than one open map, and whether closed maps are shown.

## Context

- The seed's [Packages](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#packages) section gives core two adapters, GitHub and local `.scratch`, and lists GitLab and multi-root as open in [Not yet specified](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#not-yet-specified).
- Anything cut here moves to the map's Out of scope. The shape of a GitLab or "Other" adapter is fog on the map and may graduate from this ticket's answer.
","labels":{"nodes":[{"name":"wayfinder:grilling"}]},"assignees":{"nodes":[{"login":"dbarjs"}]},"parent":{"number":1},"blockedBy":{"nodes":[]},"comments":{"nodes":[{"author":{"login":"dbarjs"},"createdAt":"2026-10-02T20:53:05Z","body":"## Answer

Decided with Eduardo in a grilling session on 2026-10-02. v0.1.0 supports two trackers and one repo per window.

### Trackers

- **In: GitHub on github.com**, with native sub-issues and native dependencies.
- **In: local markdown** under `.scratch/<effort>/`. It is the cheapest second adapter, and it keeps the snapshot from becoming GitHub-shaped: tickets are file paths, not URLs or issue numbers, and a claim has no person attached.
- **Out: GitLab.** Upstream GitLab is nearly all text conventions (`Part of #<map>`, a text blocker fallback on the free tier, an epic as the map on some tiers), and there is no GitLab project with a map to test against.
- **Out: "Other" trackers** and the agentic collect step. It would run an unattended agent with arbitrary CLIs on a timer.
- **Not promised: GitHub Enterprise Server.** The Cockpit tries any GitHub remote and shows the error if it fails.
- **Not promised: the text fallbacks** (`Part of #<map>` with a task list, `Blocked by: #n`). A map that uses them shows a drift warning.
- **Not promised: cross-repo relationships.** A map's tickets are its sub-issues in the same repo. A blocker in another repo is shown if the API returns it, and otherwise ignored.

### Which tracker a repo uses

- The **tracker doc decides**, classified by its heading (`# Issue tracker: GitHub`, `# Issue tracker: Local Markdown`) with no model. The Cockpit looks at `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` first, then follows the link in the `## Agent skills` block of `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. An unrecognized heading is an unsupported tracker.
- **One tracker per repo.** If the doc says GitHub and `.scratch/*/map.md` files also exist (or the reverse), only the tracker the doc names is read.

### When the Cockpit can't show maps

One plain message per case, with no maps. Actions that need no tracker, such as `/grill-me`, stay available in every case.

| Case | What the Cockpit shows |
| --- | --- |
| No tracker doc | Leads with `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` |
| GitLab or "Other" doc | Names the tracker and says it isn't supported yet |
| GitHub doc, remote not on github.com | Tries anyway, and shows the error if it fails |
| `gh` missing or not logged in | Shows the fix (`gh auth login`) |

### Workspace shapes

- **One repo per window.** The Cockpit names the repo it is showing.
- **Multi-root workspace:** the first workspace folder, in workspace order, whose repo root has a tracker doc. If none has one, the first folder inside a git repo, which gets the setup message. Grouping maps per folder and a repo picker are out.
- **Folder inside a repo** (such as `packages/vscode` opened alone): in. The root comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; the tracker is read from there and sessions start there.
- **Folder holding several repos:** out. The Cockpit says no repo was found.

### Several maps

- **Every open map is shown**, each with its own frontier. A finished map that is still open stays visible, since that is where `/to-spec` is offered.
- **Closed maps are neither shown nor collected.**
- **On a local tracker every `.scratch/*/map.md` is shown.** A `map.md` has no open or closed state upstream, and the Cockpit invents none; a user hides a map by removing its directory.

### Local tracker details

- **Claim.** The glossary's Claim becomes: "A ticket marked as taken, made by the session before any work: an assignee on GitHub, a `Status: claimed` line on a local tracker." The Cockpit shows who claimed a ticket only where the tracker knows.
- **Sessions run in the main checkout**, without `-w`. Whether the Cockpit limits parallel local sessions is handed to [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5).

### Where this changes the seed

- "Multi-root workspaces, repos with several maps, and a GitLab tracker adapter" is no longer open: see above.
- The "Other" tracker paragraph of the scout (an agentic collect step) is cut.
- The Language entry for Claim assumed an assignment, which a local tracker doesn't have.

### No ADR

Each cut can be reversed by adding an adapter or a view later, so none of these meets the bar.

### Not yet done

The Claim wording above is not on `main` yet. This session's checkout was on another session's `prototype/map-rendering` branch, and the push to `main` was not permitted from here.

Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-02. v0.1.0 ships the VS Code extension and nothing else.

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `@hero-synergy/cli` | Cut from v0.1.0. No commands ship, and the spec removes `packages/cli` from the workspace. |
| `@hero-synergy/core` | Internal. It stays a separate workspace package with `"private": true` and no `vscode` imports, bundled into the extension and never published. |

- **Core stays its own package** so that "no `vscode` imports" is enforced by the package boundary, its tests run under plain `vp test`, and a later CLI or public release is a manifest change.

A Cockpit session runs in its own worktree (`claude -w <ticket-slug>`). Grilling tickets edit `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs inline, so those edits land in the worktree. How do they get back to `main`, and who cleans up?

To decide:

- Whether every session gets a worktree, or only some ticket types.
- How glossary and ADR edits reach `main`: a commit straight to `main`, a branch and PR per ticket, or something the Cockpit offers as an action.
- What happens when two sessions edit `CONTEXT.md` at the same time.
- Who removes worktrees, and what the Cockpit shows about them.
- The local `.scratch` tracker exception: the seed says to run without `-w` there, or claims land in a private copy of the map.

## Context

- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) in the seed.
- Until this is resolved, this map runs on the standing rule in its Notes: sessions commit glossary and ADR edits straight to `main`. The answer here replaces that rule.
- The session lifecycle (resume, one live session per ticket, AFK tickets) is fog on the map and may graduate from this ticket's answer.
","labels":{"nodes":[{"name":"wayfinder:grilling"}]},"assignees":{"nodes":[{"login":"dbarjs"}]},"parent":{"number":1},"blockedBy":{"nodes":[]},"comments":{"nodes":[{"author":{"login":"dbarjs"},"createdAt":"2026-10-02T22:00:20Z","body":"## Resolution

**Every ticket session runs in its own worktree and pushes its own edits to `main`; the Cockpit only shows worktree state.** Eduardo agreed to all eleven points on 2026-10-02. This replaces the standing rule in the map's Notes.

Recorded in [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md), the **Worktree** glossary term in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md), and the push-back routine in [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

### Decided

1. **The Cockpit launches and watches.** It never runs git (no worktree creation, merge-back or removal) and never writes to the tracker. The push-back convention lives in the repo's own docs; hero-synergy's README recommends it, nothing writes it into the user's repo. ADR 0003.
2. **Every ticket session gets `-w <slug>`**, grilling included: today's shared checkout had an uncommitted `CONTEXT.md` edit from one session and sat 3 commits behind `origin/main` under another, which is exactly the collision. Standalone actions (`/grill-me`, `/ask-matt`, chart a map) run in the workspace root without `-w`.
3. **Glossary and ADR edits reach `main` by direct push, no PR:** in the worktree, `pnpm install`, `pnpm exec vp run build` (core's types come from `dist/`, so `vp check` fails unbuilt), edit, `pnpm exec vp check --fix`, commit on the worktree branch, `git pull --rebase origin main`, `git push origin HEAD:main` at ticket close. Prototype work stays on `prototype/<name>`, research on `research/<name>`, both pushed.
4. **Concurrent `CONTEXT.md` edits** are accepted: the session that pushes second rebases and resolves the conflict. No serialization of grilling sessions.
5. **Local `.scratch` tracker: no `-w`.** `.scratch` is gitignored, so a worktree has no tracker in it; `.worktreeinclude` would only copy it, and claims would still land in a private map. The Cockpit shows a note that sessions share the checkout; no enforcement of one session at a time.
6. **The Cockpit shows each ticket's worktree** (read-only, via `git worktree list` and `git log main..<branch>`): exists, has uncommitted files, has commits not on `main`. The last one is "work that never made it back".
7. **Branch name is the native `worktree-<slug>`.** A `WorktreeCreate` hook would replace all of claude's worktree logic for the sake of a nicer name.
8. **The exit prompt is an accepted gap**, like Esc: every `-n` session, clean or not, asks keep-or-remove on `/exit`, and no hook sees it. The Cockpit shows time since the last status event.
9. **Removal** is claude's exit prompt (remove once pushed, keep if unpushed) or the developer's hand. Nothing removes a worktree automatically; leftovers stay listed with their state (point 6).

### Facts that shaped it

From the [worktrees doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md): `-w` creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>` on `worktree-<name>`, branched from the **remote** default branch (`worktree.baseRef: "fresh"`), so a session never starts from a stale local `main`. `--resume` returns to the worktree. Headless `-p` runs never prompt and leave the worktree in place. No built-in push-back or merge-back exists.

### Not decided here

Resuming, one live session per ticket, AFK tickets and the workspace trust dialog graduate to their own ticket on the map.

**A tree of maps with a focus pane, no graph.** Eduardo picked it on 2026-10-02 after reacting to seven variants, as the merge of two of them ("M2 One tree" and "C List + focus"), and accepted the final shape for v0.1.0.

Prototype, all variants and the README: [`prototype/map-rendering`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/prototype/map-rendering/packages/vscode/webview/src/prototype) (`cd packages/vscode && pnpm run prototype`, then `?variant=M4`). Fed by this repo's own map plus 44 invented maps, because Eduardo's repos normally hold many maps, most of them finished (one project: 45 maps, about 85% done).

### Decided

1. **One tree for all maps**, like the file explorer. Each open map is a node showing its number, title, how many sessions need you, how many tickets are takeable (or ⊘ when nothing is), and decided/total. Maps are ordered: a session needs you first, then something takeable, then stuck.
2. **A map row only unfolds.** Inside it, in this order: a **⚑ Map** item, the open tickets (claimed with their session status first, then the frontier with its first ticket marked `next`, then blocked tickets with `waits on #n #m` inline), then a folded **≋ Fog** node and a folded **✓ Decisions so far** node.
3. **A focus pane shows whatever is clicked**, and nothing is shown until something is. A ticket shows: type and HITL/AFK, state and claim, its title as a link that opens the issue (GitHub URL, or the markdown file on a local tracker), a two-column neighbourhood "Waits on → Clears the way for" (tickets and fog, each clickable), the decision gist if closed, the live session with its status and time since the last status event, and for a frontier ticket the **Work ticket** action with the exact command. No question text: the issue is one click away. The ⚑ Map item shows the destination, the decisions folded, and out of scope.
4. **Two widths, one component.** At editor-tab width the pane sits to the right of the tree. At sidebar width it sits inline under the clicked row, and a second click on the row or ✕ closes it. Where the Cockpit lives is still open, see below.

**Yes.** Full findings, with the working query and a sample of its output: [`docs/research/scout-graphql-query.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/scout-graphql-query/docs/research/scout-graphql-query.md) on the `research/scout-graphql-query` branch.

One `gh api graphql` query returns everything the collect step needs, with no preview header. Run against this repo's map it returned all 20 issues in one request (1.6 s, 40 KB, 6 rate-limit points), with children, labels, assignees and blocking edges correct.

- **Fields.** `parent`, `subIssues`, `subIssuesSummary`, `blockedBy`, `blocking`, `issueDependenciesSummary`, `labels`, `assignees`, `body`, `comments(last: n)`, `state`, `updatedAt`.
- **Selection.** `repository.issues(labels: [...])` matches the list as an OR and ignores names that don't exist, so the scout passes the known label names explicitly. Prefix and wildcard matching work nowhere, search included. `repository.labels(query: "wayfinder:")` in the same request lists the wayfinder labels that exist.
- **Pagination.** Only the top-level `issues` connection paginates, at 100 per page. Sub-issues cap at 100 per parent and dependencies at 50 per relationship, so the nested connections fit in one page.
- **Cost.** 6 points per page of 100, against 5,000 per hour. The cost depends on the page size, not on how many issues exist. A refresh every minute uses about 7% of the budget.
- **REST.** It has no data that GraphQL lacks. Its only extras are conditional requests (a 304 is free) and a separate rate-limit bucket; as a fallback it takes 13 requests for this map instead of 1.

## Where the seed is wrong

- **`updatedAt` does not move when a parent or a blocker is added.** On [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16), `updatedAt` still equals `createdAt` although the parent and two blockers were added afterwards. So `updatedAt` is a safe cache key for interpreting bodies and comments only; relationships must come from every fresh collect.
- **"One query" holds per 100 issues.** Closed tickets keep their labels, so a repo with several finished maps needs pagination, and the seed's pipe into `claude -p` assumes a single page.
- **The seed's sample command passes no variables**, but the label names have to be passed explicitly.
- The ticket's premise that REST gives something GraphQL doesn't was wrong.

## Not verified

- **Map order.** Whether `subIssues` comes back in map order. It returned the tickets in creation order, which here is the same thing. The frontier's "first in map order" depends on this.
- **Closed blockers.** Whether a closed blocker stays in `blockedBy`. Every blocker was open at the time; the query selects each blocker's `state` so the scout can decide either way.
- **`updatedAt` on other events**, such as a new comment or a blocker closing.
- **A real 50-ticket map.** The cost is certain; time and size were estimated from another repo (100 issues took 6.7 s, close to GitHub's 10 s cut-off).
- **GitHub Enterprise Server** and cross-repository parents or blockers.

Full findings: [`docs/research/wayfinder-conventions.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/wayfinder-conventions/docs/research/wayfinder-conventions.md) on the `research/wayfinder-conventions` branch. Everything comes from the git history of `mattpocock/skills` (`main` at `d81f3a1`, 2026-09-29) and the installed plugin, 1.2.3.

Upstream has shipped three generations of wayfinder state:

1. **A single Markdown file** (the `decision-mapping` skill, 2026-06-15 to 2026-07-01), with tickets as sections carrying `Type:`, `Status:` and `Blocked by:` lines.
2. **An early tracker map** (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-05, never in a tagged release): a `wayfinder:map` issue with a Notes / Decisions so far / Fog body.
3. **The current tracker map** (since 2026-07-05, released in v1.1.0 on 2026-07-08): Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope.

What a program can rely on:

- **Map body.** Four heading sets existed within four days. Recognize the old ones by their H2 headings: `Fog` without `Destination`, or `Deferred`; today's body has `Not yet specified`.
- **Claim.** The `wayfinder:claimed` label lived for 39 hours on `main` and was never released. Since then any assignee is the claim. On a local tracker the claim is a `Status: claimed` line, and always has been.
- **Ticket types.** The four `wayfinder:<type>` labels arrived together and were never renamed.
- **Fallbacks**, unchanged since the start: `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body plus a task list in the map body on GitHub, and `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` at the top of the child body. GitLab always uses `Part of #<map>`.
- **Local layout.** `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` and `issues/NN-<slug>.md` with `Type:`, `Status: claimed|resolved`, `Blocked by: NN, NN`, and the answer under `## Answer`.
- **Decisions so far entries.** `- [title](link) — gist` up to 1.2.3; unreleased `main` writes `- [title](link): gist`.
- **Upstream disagrees with itself today.** All three tracker templates still name the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body, while `SKILL.md` uses the five current headings.

## Where the seed is wrong

- `wayfinder:claimed` was never in a tagged release, so legacy claim labels are a rare case, not a common one.
- No tracker ever had a three-type label set: `task` is older than the labels.
- "The assignee is the claim" does not hold on a local tracker.
- The collect step can't assume `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`: since v1.1.0 upstream finds the tracker doc through the pointer in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
- "Labels decide what the scout sees" is too strong: setup never creates the labels, a GitLab map may be an epic, and a local tracker has no labels.

## Not verified

- How common each legacy form is on real trackers: only upstream history and this repo's own map were read.

- Whether exec-form hooks (`command: node`, `args`) and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` paths work on Windows.
- Whether appending to and watching the events file behaves the same there.

## Context

- See [Sessions](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#sessions) and [Live status](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/seed.md#live-status) in the seed.

","labels":{"nodes":[{"name":"wayfinder:research"}]},"assignees":{"nodes":[{"login":"dbarjs"}]},"parent":{"number":1},"blockedBy":{"nodes":[]},"comments":{"nodes":[{"author":{"login":"dbarjs"},"createdAt":"2026-10-02T19:38:14Z","body":"## Answer

Full findings, with twelve concrete Windows test items: [`docs/research/windows-behavior.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/windows-behavior/docs/research/windows-behavior.md) on the `research/windows-behavior` branch. This was reading only; nothing was run on Windows.

What breaks or needs different handling:

- **How `claude` is installed changes how it can be spawned.** Claude Code runs natively (PowerShell or cmd; Git Bash is optional since 2.1.120) or inside WSL. The native install is `claude.exe`, but an npm install is a `claude.cmd` / `claude.ps1` shim, which Node's `child_process` can't spawn without a shell. This affects the scout as well as sessions.
- **The seed's launch command is bash syntax.** `sendText` does no quoting, and PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash each quote the ticket title and the prompt differently.
- **Running `claude` as the terminal's process avoids the quoting.** With `shellPath: 'claude'` and a `shellArgs` array, VS Code resolves the binary through `PATH` and node-pty quotes each argument, so no shell is involved.
- **Git Bash may rewrite the `/wayfinder …` prompt** into a Windows path, because of MSYS argument conversion.
- **Environment variables are fine.** `TerminalOptions.env` is shell-independent and hooks inherit the session's environment.
- **The hook shape in the seed is the one the docs recommend for Windows.** Exec-form `node` with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` needs Claude Code 2.1.139 or later and a real `node.exe` on `PATH`.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`** (2.1.280 and later) can replace `--plugin-dir "<path>"` and remove one quoted path.
- **`SessionEnd` probably never fires when a terminal is closed.** Windows kills the process forcefully, so "ended" should come from `window.onDidCloseTerminal`.
- **Watching the events file needs care.** Appending behaves the same as elsewhere, but watcher events are coalesced and can be dropped, so read from a byte offset, add a slow poll, and create the file before watching.
- **WSL remote windows behave as Linux.** Claude Code and Node must be installed inside the distribution.

## Against the seed

Nothing contradicts a seed decision. The gaps:

- The Sessions command doesn't say whether it is typed into a shell or run as the terminal's process.
- "SessionEnd means ended" can't be the only source of that status.
- The status plugin needs Claude Code 2.1.139 or later and `node` on `PATH`; the seed states neither, and Claude Code itself doesn't require Node.
- The scout example is a bash pipeline and needs a rule for npm `.cmd` installs. An open user report says `claude.cmd` broke a `--json-schema` call that `claude.exe` handled.

## Needs a real Windows test

- Whether exec-form hooks really bypass Git Bash: the maintainer's confirmation was on Linux, and two user reports describe arguments being re-parsed.
- Whether `shellPath: 'claude'` starts at all with only the npm shim.
- Whether Git Bash converts the `/wayfinder …` argument.
- Whether `SessionEnd` produces a status event on any Windows exit path.
- How cmd treats `%`, `^`, `!` and quotes in a ticket title; no primary source was found.

Full findings: [`docs/research/fork-vscode-versions.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/fork-vscode-versions/docs/research/fork-vscode-versions.md) on the `research/fork-vscode-versions` branch. Everything was read on 2026-10-02; nothing was run inside any fork.

| Editor | Current release | VS Code version it declares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | 1.140.0 (2026-09-30) | 1.140.0 |
| VSCodium | 1.135.06055 | 1.135.0 |
| Cursor | 3.23.12 | 1.128.0 |
| Windsurf (named Devin Desktop since 2026-06-02) | 3.10.48 | 1.126.0 |

**Recommended floor: `"engines": { "vscode": "^1.105.0" }` with `"@types/vscode": "~1.105.0"`.**

- **Node sets the floor, not the APIs.** Every API the Cockpit needs exists by VS Code 1.93. But VS Code 1.100 runs extensions on Node 20.19, below the `>=22.18` the seed sets for the core package the extension bundles. 1.104 is the first on Node 22.18, and 1.105 is the first such version that the forks actually shipped.
- **The floor can't go above 1.126**, the version Windsurf is on. `^1.125.0` with `~1.125.0` is the alternative if a Node 24 extension host is wanted; it drops fork builds from before July 2026.
- **When each API landed.** `createFileSystemWatcher` 1.0, `TerminalOptions.name` 1.9, `env` 1.18, `WebviewView` 1.50, `iconPath` 1.58, `color` 1.60, `location` (terminal in the editor area) 1.64, `isTransient` 1.65, shell integration 1.93. Watching a path outside the workspace needs a `RelativePattern` (1.64).
- **How the forks lag.** VS Code has shipped weekly since 1.111 (March 2026), so a gap of N versions is about N weeks. Cursor and Windsurf rebase irregularly: they land 2 to 7 weeks behind, then drift to 6.5 to 8.5 months. VSCodium follows within two weeks but now skips most weekly releases.
- **Pin `@types/vscode` with a tilde.** vsce 4.0.0 fails packaging if the types' major.minor exceeds `engines.vscode`, but it only reads the manifest string, so a caret range passes and still installs 1.140 types.
- **`@types/vscode` is no longer published for every release.** After 1.110 only some versions exist (1.115, 1.116, 1.118, 1.120, 1.125, 1.134, 1.136, 1.137, 1.138, 1.140), so a pin such as `~1.126.0` resolves to nothing.

## Against the seed

- The placeholder `^1.100.0` conflicts with the seed's own Node requirement, as above.
- "Windsurf" is now Devin Desktop.

## Not verified

- **Behavior inside the forks.** The versions are what each build declares, and Cursor staff say the editor internals "can sit on an older base" than the declared API version. Terminal in the editor area, terminal icons and webview views need a real test in each fork.
- **Cursor's exact switch dates.** Eleven builds were sampled; its changelog announces only one base change.
- **Windsurf's history** relies on its changelog, so an unannounced base change would be missing.
- **Node versions in the forks** come from Linux x64 builds only.

The workable options:

| Option | What it covers | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit and component tests in `vp test` | Core, the extension's pure logic, and the Vue webview with `acquireVsCodeApi()` stubbed (happy-dom or jsdom with `@vue/test-utils`, or Vitest Browser Mode) | None beyond the stack, except Browser Mode's Playwright dependency |

- **Vitest can't run inside the extension host through any first-party route.** The official CLI "exclusively uses Mocha". The one community pool for Vitest is immature (version 0.1.3, built on an experimental API, older than Vitest 5).
- **Extension-host tests run on VS Code's bundled Node**, not Node 26: 20.19 at VS Code 1.100.
- **Webview contents can't be reached from extension-host tests.**
- **Every surveyed extension** (vitest-dev/vscode, oxc-vscode, cline, vscode-copilot-chat) uses Mocha through `vscode-test` for the host and Vitest for everything else. None uses WebdriverIO, ExTester or the Vitest pool.
- **CI.** xvfb is preinstalled on `ubuntu-latest`. The VS Code download is about 349 MB and most repos don't cache it.

- **"Use `vp` for everything" can't cover extension-host tests.** They need Mocha started by `vscode-test`, launched through `vp run`, not `vp test`.
- **New dependencies.** `@vscode/test-cli`, `@vscode/test-electron` and `@types/mocha` are outside the Stack table, so the working agreement calls for an ADR.
- **The CI workflow has no display server**; an integration step needs `xvfb-run -a`.
- **Compiled tests need their own output directory**, because `dist` is cleaned by `vp pack` and shipped through `files`.

**Yes.** `@effect/vitest` 4.0.0 runs under the Vitest 5.0.1 that Vite+ 1.0.0 bundles, with no override and no peer-dependency warning.

### What was done

On the throwaway branch [`task/effect-vitest`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/tree/task/effect-vitest) (commit b20ff17, not for `main`):

- Added `effect@4.0.0` (dependency) and `@effect/vitest@4.0.0` (devDependency) to `packages/core`.
- Wrote [`packages/core/src/effect.test.ts`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/task/effect-vitest/packages/core/src/effect.test.ts): `it.effect`, `it.live`, `it.effect.each`, `.fails`, `.skip`, `.prop` (from a Schema), the `TestClock`, the Vitest test context, and a shared `layer(...)`.
- Ran `vp run -r build`, `vp check`, `vp test` and the extension typecheck.

### Result

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `vp test`, Node 26.10 | 2 files passed; 12 passed, 1 expected fail, 1 skipped |
| `vp test`, Node 24.20 | same |
| `vp check` (format, type-aware lint, type check with TypeScript 7) | passes after `vp check --fix` |
| `vp run -r build`, extension typecheck | pass |
| A deliberately failing `it.effect` | reported as a failed test, exit code 1, the typed error printed |

### Facts later tickets can rely on

- **Peer dependencies.** `@effect/vitest` peers on `vitest >=5.0.0 <6.0.0` and `effect ^4.0.0`. `packages/core` does not declare `vitest`; pnpm satisfies the peer with the `vitest@5.0.1` that `vite-plus` already depends on. `pnpm peers check` reports no issues and `pnpm why vitest` finds one version.

- **`effect@4.0.0` has no dependencies**, and `TestClock` lives in `effect/testing`.
- **Formatting.** `pnpm add` writes the new `package.json` keys in an order Oxfmt rejects; run `vp check --fix` after adding a dependency.

### One risk, no action needed now

The single instance holds because pnpm reused the Vitest already in the lockfile (5.0.1) even though 5.0.3 is the latest. If a later install ever resolves the peer to a different Vitest than the one Vite+ pins, `it.effect` would register tests with a second copy and they would silently not run. The "one Vitest instance" test in the spike catches this; the fix would be a `vitest` entry in the pnpm catalog or overrides matching Vite+'s pin. `@effect/vitest` 4.0.0 itself was built against Vitest 5.0.2.

[zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/15) can now treat Effect Schema as testable in this toolchain; tooling is not a reason to prefer zod.

**Effect Schema models all boundary data, and zod is dropped from the stack.** Eduardo's rule was: if Effect Schema completely replaces zod, use it. It does. Recorded in [ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md).

- **One library.** Effect Schema models the snapshot, config, webview messages, status events and `SKILL.md` frontmatter. This overrides the seed's `[E]` requirement for zod.
- **The webview doesn't validate.** It imports types only. The host and webview ship in one `.vsix`, and the host validates messages arriving from the webview.
- **Boundary data is plain JSON.** Timestamps stay ISO strings and schemas don't transform, so the decoded and encoded shapes are the same.
- **`@hero-synergy/core` doesn't export schema objects.** It exports types and functions that parse. Webview message schemas live in `packages/vscode`. Core stays private in v0.1.0 (see [What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/4)), so this rule is cheap to change until core is published.

### The ticket's three questions

Measured on 2026-10-02 with Effect 4.0.0, zod 4.6.5 and Claude Code 2.1.287.

- **Modeling twice?** No, with either choice. Effect code carries a zod-inferred type like any other type. The Effect modules the scout needs (child processes, file system, scheduling) don't import Schema; only the persistence modules do.
- **JSON Schema for `claude -p --json-schema`?** Both work on Haiku, each with one adjustment.
  - Effect: `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument()` returns `{ dialect, schema, definitions }`. Pass `schema` with `definitions` moved under `$defs`. Shared definitions, descriptions, optional and nullable fields and records were all accepted.
  - zod: the raw `z.toJSONSchema()` output is rejected with `no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"`. It is accepted once `$schema` is removed, or with `target: "draft-7"`.
- **Webview bundle cost?** For validating one three-variant message (esbuild, minified):

| Webview validates with | Minified | Gzipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zod | 88.3 KB | 25.9 KB |
| Effect Schema | 74.5 KB | 24.9 KB |
| zod/mini | 23.1 KB | 7.6 KB |
| Nothing (types only) | 0 | 0 |

v0.1.0 promises **VS Code 1.105 or later on macOS and Linux**, with native Windows and the VS Code forks reachable but untested. The whole promise is one **Requirements** section in `packages/vscode/README.md`, which the Marketplace and Open VSX render, plus the `engines` field.

### Operating systems

| Platform | Tier | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (arm64, x64) | Supported | Tested by hand before a release. |
| Linux (arm64, x64), including dev containers and SSH remotes | Supported | CI runs here; the devcontainer is the development environment. |
| WSL remote window on a Windows host | Supported, as Linux | `extensionKind: workspace` puts the scout, `gh` and `claude` inside the distribution. **This is the documented route for Windows users.** |
| Native Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash) | Best-effort | The code avoids every trap the Windows research found, the README says "untested on Windows", Windows bugs are accepted but never block a release. Install Claude Code with the **native installer**, not npm. |

One universal `.vsix`: the extension bundles no native modules.

### Editors

- `"engines": { "vscode": "^1.105.0" }` and `"@types/vscode": "~1.105.0"` (exists on npm; the `@types/vscode` gaps start after 1.110). The floor is set by Node, not by any API: every API the Cockpit uses exists since 1.93, but 1.105 is the first version that both runs extensions on Node ≥ 22.18 (core's own engine) and that every fork has shipped. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) on 1.126 is the ceiling the floor must stay under.
- The pin is a tilde because vsce 4 reads only the manifest string: a caret would pass packaging and still install 1.140 types.
- **Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium are not blocked, not supported.** The `.vsix` is published to **Open VSX** (namespace `dbarjs`, decided in #19), the README says "built for VS Code; forks are expected to work", and fork bugs are accepted, not promised. The fork research could not verify terminal-in-editor-area, terminal icons or webview views inside any fork, and Cursor staff say the internals can sit on an older base than the declared version.

### Runtime requirements the README states

- **Claude Code ≥ 2.1.139**, the release that added exec-form hooks (`"args": [...]`, no shell), the newest feature the status plugin relies on. `SessionEnd` is 1.0.85, `PermissionRequest` 2.0.45, `StopFailure` 2.1.78, `async: true` predates 2.1.23. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` (2.1.280) is not used: with the launch below, `--plugin-dir <path>` is never shell-quoted, so the variable would only raise the floor.
- **Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH`** in the session's environment, because the hooks run `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/report.mjs` and Claude Code itself ships no Node. On Windows that means a real `node.exe`. Handing the session the extension host's Node instead is a possible later refinement, not a v0.1.0 question.
- `gh` authenticated, for the GitHub tracker (already implied by #3).

### Decisions this forces on the launch

- **A session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process**: `createTerminal({ shellPath: 'claude', shellArgs: [...] })`, never a command typed into a shell with `sendText`. VS Code resolves the binary on `PATH` and node-pty quotes each argument, so the ticket title and the `/wayfinder …` prompt never pass through PowerShell, cmd or Git Bash (which would otherwise rewrite the slash-command as a path). Consequences accepted: the terminal closes when `claude` exits, which is the "ended" signal #6 chose; there is no shell for follow-up commands in that terminal; shell integration is unavailable. Feeds #21.
- **The extension resolves `claude` on `PATH` itself** for the scout and the launch, and on Windows prefers `claude.exe`; an npm `.cmd` shim can't be spawned by `child_process` without a shell, so it's best-effort only.
- **No gating on editor or OS.** The extension activates everywhere the floor allows, with no warning on forks or Windows. On activation it writes `vscode.env.appName`, `appHost`, the VS Code version, `process.platform` and the resolved `claude` path to the Cockpit's output channel, so bug reports from a fork or Windows carry what the research could not verify.

### Not an ADR

None of this is hard to reverse: the floor is a manifest number, the tiers are README text, and the `shellPath` launch is a few lines. The reasoning lives here; the `createTerminal` call gets a code comment when it's built.

### Out of scope, after v0.1.0

- The twelve-item real-Windows test from [`docs/research/windows-behavior.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/research/windows-behavior/docs/research/windows-behavior.md).
- Verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside each fork.

Sources: #11 and #12, and the Claude Code changelog read on 2026-10-02 (latest release 2.1.288).

**Every tier is in: the harness is a first-class deliverable of v0.1.0.** Eduardo's steer on 2026-10-02 was "the harness is very important, add test for everything", and he accepted every point below as recommended. The research that fed this ticket is [How can a VS Code extension be integration-tested under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/13); the runners decision is recorded as [ADR 0004](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-extension-host-tests-run-on-mocha-beside-vitest.md).

### Decided

1. **Four tiers.**

   | Tier | Runner | Entry point | Covers |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Unit | Vitest (`@effect/vitest` for Effect code) | `vp test` | `@hero-synergy/core`, the extension's pure logic, the session status plugin |
   | Component | Vitest + happy-dom + `@vue/test-utils` | `vp test` | The Cockpit's Vue app outside VS Code, `acquireVsCodeApi()` stubbed |
   | Extension host | Mocha through `@vscode/test-cli` + `@vscode/test-electron` | `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` | Activation, the view resolving, terminals, the real `vscode` API |
   | End-to-end | Vitest `e2e` project launching VS Code through `playwright._electron` | `vp test --project e2e` | The whole path, including the Cockpit inside its webview |

   Playwright is a library here, not a runner: two runners total (Vitest, Mocha), never three. `vp test` with no `--project` excludes `e2e`, so the fast loop stays fast. `retry: 1` on the `e2e` project only; zero retries everywhere else.

2. **The seam in the extension package.** `vscode` is imported only in adapter modules under `packages/vscode/src/vscode/`. Everything else is pure TypeScript or an Effect service whose live `Layer` imports `vscode` and whose test `Layer` is in-memory (terminals, the webview, the events-file watcher, workspace folders). Host tests cover the adapters; the bulk is unit-tested. This is a working-agreement rule in the map's Notes.

3. **`gh` and `claude -p` in core.** One process-runner Effect service with a live layer and a replay layer. Real `gh api graphql` and `claude -p --json-schema` outputs are recorded once (this repo's own maps as the subject), checked in under `packages/core/test/fixtures/`, and replayed; they also pin the exact GraphQL shape the one-query decision depends on. Plus **one live `gh` job** in CI against this repo's own maps with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (6 rate-limit points per run), **non-blocking for merge**, to catch GitHub changing the sub-issue or dependency API shape. `claude -p` stays fixture-only.

4. **The session status plugin.** Both sides: a unit test spawns `node claude-plugin/report.mjs` with `HERO_SYNERGY_TICKET` and `HERO_SYNERGY_EVENTS` set and a hook payload on stdin, then asserts the appended status event; the extension's reader is tested on recorded event files. Payloads and files come from the status-hooks prototype's recorded runs, so the corrected six-row table from [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6) is pinned by tests, including out-of-order `SessionEnd` and `/clear` starting a new session id. Neither needs Claude Code installed.

5. **Faking `claude` and `gh` for host and end-to-end tests.** Both mechanisms: a user-facing setting for the `claude` location (nvm and Homebrew users need it anyway) that tests point at a stub, and stub executables in `test/fixtures/bin/` on `PATH` for the one test that proves the default lookup works. The stub `claude` records its argv and writes status events on a script (started, working, waiting for you, ended), so live status is driven end-to-end. The fixture workspace uses the **local markdown tracker**, so the map needs no `gh` at all; the stub `gh` covers the GitHub path with the same recorded fixtures as core.

6. **VS Code builds.** Host and end-to-end tests run on **both** the floor (`1.105.0`, the promise made in [Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/17)) and the newest stable, as an array in `.vscode-test.mjs`.

7. **Coverage.** Report now (`vp test --coverage`, the number visible in CI); a failing threshold comes in its own ticket after the first implementation lands, because picking a number now is picking it blind. Coverage applies to the Vitest tiers only.

8. **CI runners and jobs.** Linux for every tier, **macOS for host and end-to-end** (the terminal and the `claude` spawn are the OS-specific surface; the repo is public, so macOS minutes are free). Three parallel jobs: `check` (build, lint, types, unit, component), `vscode` (host and end-to-end on Linux under `xvfb-run -a` and on macOS, the VS Code download cached by OS and version), `live` (the `gh` job). `check` and `vscode` are required for merge; `live` is not.

9. **House rules.** The "use `vp` for everything" rule now reads: every test runs through a `vp` command, `vp test` for Vitest and `vp run --filter hero-synergy test:integration` for the extension host; never call `vitest`, `mocha` or `vscode-test` directly. The adapter rule from point 2 joins it. ADR 0004 records the two runners and the stack additions: `@vscode/test-cli`, `@vscode/test-electron`, `@types/mocha`, `playwright`, `happy-dom`, `@vue/test-utils`.

### Ruled out for v0.1.0

A Windows CI runner (native Windows is best-effort and the real-Windows test is already out of scope); Insiders builds; a live `claude -p` job (no credentials in CI, and the interpret step is still open); Vitest Browser Mode (end-to-end already covers real rendering, and its provider must be pinned to Vite+'s exact Vitest); Playwright Test, `vitest-environment-vscode`, `wdio-vscode-service` and ExTester as runners.

### Defaults for the spec

Not decisions; `/to-spec` may change them freely.

- Host tests in `packages/vscode/test/integration/**/*.test.ts`, bundled to CommonJS by a second `pack` entry into `out-test/` (gitignored, outside `files`, so neither cleaned by `vp pack` nor shipped in the VSIX), with their own tsconfig so `@types/mocha` globals don't leak into Vitest files. `.vscode-test.mjs` with `mocha: { ui: 'bdd' }`, `node:assert/strict`, `launchArgs: ['--disable-extensions']`, and a `workspaceFolder` pointing at the fixture workspace.
- End-to-end tests in `packages/vscode/test/e2e/`, the VS Code download shared with the host tests through `@vscode/test-electron`'s `.vscode-test/` cache (gitignored and ignored by lint and format).
- The fixture workspace in `packages/vscode/test/fixtures/workspace/`: a `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` naming the local markdown tracker and a `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` with a few tickets.
- `.vscode/launch.json` with an `extensionHost` configuration whose `testConfiguration` points at `.vscode-test.mjs`, so the Extension Test Runner extension and the debugger work locally.

### Not verified

Nothing here has been run; the research was reading only. Whether `vp pack` with an array `pack` block produces `.cjs` files that `vscode-test` loads, whether a Vitest project can launch Electron under `vp test`, and whether ESM test files load in the host are proved by the task ticket [Do the two test runners coexist under Vite+?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/25) before `/to-spec` depends on them.

### Pipeline

The spine of the seed's `release.yml` (A.3) was built around npm and goes:

## Why

- **All three, because each does a different job.** The Marketplace is where VS Code users look, Open VSX is the only route to the forks, and the `.vsix` on the release is what works when neither registry does. None of them costs a release day.
- **The release never waits for a registry** because the `.vsix` is the fallback: a Marketplace hiccup or a slow Open VSX claim leaving users with nothing would defeat the point of attaching it.

- **Resume.** When a ticket's terminal closes, what the Cockpit offers: `claude --resume "<ticket title>"` (which returns to the worktree by itself), a fresh launch, or both; and how the Cockpit tells "ended on purpose" from "terminal died".
- **One live session per ticket.** How the Cockpit holds to it when a ticket is claimed on the tracker but no terminal is open here, or a terminal is open but the tracker shows the ticket unclaimed. Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`.

## Context

- Graduated from the map's fog by [How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/5) and bound by [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md): the Cockpit launches and watches, never runs git or writes to the tracker.

**A ticket's session is none, starting, live or ended; liveness comes from the Cockpit's terminal and from Claude Code's own session registry; Resume is `--resume <session id>` with the id learned from the status events; every ticket runs in a terminal and `--bg` is cut; performance means VS Code stays responsive and the battery untouched.** Eduardo agreed to all eighteen points on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03.

### Decided

1. **Session, redefined.** A Session is one live `claude` process for a ticket or action, in a VS Code terminal, whoever started it. The conversation claude persists is not a Session: it is what Resume takes as an argument. A ticket's session state is **none**, **starting** (a terminal exists, no `SessionStart` yet), **live** (status from the table in [Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/6)) or **ended** (no process, last session id known). A ticket claimed on the tracker with no session and no known id shows as **claimed elsewhere**; its only actions are opening the issue and a fresh launch, which wayfinder accepts for a named ticket.
2. **Liveness has two sources.** The Cockpit's own terminal is its handle when it has one. Claude Code's live-session registry (`claude agents --json`: pid, cwd, session id, `-n` name, `busy|idle|waiting`) decides liveness for everything else: hand-started sessions, sessions in another window, and a process that exited non-zero while VS Code keeps the pane open with an exit alert, where `onDidCloseTerminal` never fires. The files under `~/.claude/sessions/` are never parsed: a watcher on that directory is the trigger, the documented command is the reader, debounced one second or more.
3. **The name is the key.** Session names are `#<number> <title>`; a session matches a ticket by the leading `#<number>` within the repo. It holds on both trackers, survives `/clear` (the id changes, the name doesn't) and matches hand-started sessions that follow the convention, which the README states. Claude renames a second live session with the same name to `<name>-<two words>`, so the prefix still matches; the Cockpit shows both under the ticket with a warning and kills nothing. The worktree path is corroboration in the focus pane, never the key.
4. **One live session per ticket.** While a ticket is starting or live its only action is "focus terminal" (none when the live session isn't one of the Cockpit's terminals). The Cockpit never launches a second.
5. **Ended is one state.** Its detail is text, in order of trust: the `SessionEnd` reason (`prompt_input_exit` → "exited", `logout`, `other`); else the terminal's `exitStatus` (`User` → "terminal closed", `Shutdown` → "window closed", `Process` with a non-zero code → "exited with code N"); else "process gone" when only the registry noticed. `clear` and `resume` reasons never end a ticket: the next `SessionStart` in the same terminal carries the new id. No separate crashed state, and the actions don't branch on the detail.
6. **Resume is by id.** The id is the `session_id` of the ticket's last status event; nothing is passed at launch (`--session-id` is not used), so `/clear` tracking comes for free. The command runs in a fresh terminal from the workspace root with `HERO_SYNERGY_*` set again: `claude --resume <uuid> -n "#21 <title>" --plugin-dir <ext>/claude-plugin`. Claude returns to the worktree by itself; `--plugin-dir` is not restored by claude, so the Cockpit passes it again. With no known id the action is **Resume by name**, labelled so: `claude --resume "#21 <title>"`, resolved by claude (exact match resumes, an ambiguous one opens its picker).
7. **Ended actions**: Resume first, Launch fresh second, both with their command shown, no confirmation. Launch fresh is the plain Work ticket command; `-w <slug>` reopens an existing worktree.
8. **Reload and close.** On activation the Cockpit adopts any terminal whose name starts with `#<number>` as that ticket's terminal (claude sets the terminal title to the `-n` name; VS Code keeps the processes alive across a reload but hands back no env or args), and the registry confirms it is live. 9. **Live with no events** (hand-started, or the plugin failed to load): shown as "live · <registry word>", unmapped. Mapping `busy/idle/waiting` onto the status table belongs to [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28).
10. **No `--bg` in v0.1.0.** Every ticket, AFK or HITL, runs in a terminal; an AFK ticket is a terminal you don't have to watch. The Cockpit never starts one on its own (principle 3).
11. **Local tracker launch**: `claude -n "#NN <title>" --plugin-dir <ext>/claude-plugin "/wayfinder .scratch/<effort>/map.md .scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md"`, without `-w`, cwd the workspace root, paths relative to it, `NN` from the file prefix. 12. **Dialogs no hook reports.** Starting shows its age and, after 15 s without `SessionStart`, a hint: "no status yet, the session may be waiting at a prompt, open the terminal". The keep-or-remove prompt at `/exit` stays under the last event, "waiting for you", with its age. No terminal scraping. The Cockpit never edits `hasTrustDialogAccepted` in claude's config.
13. **Starting counts as live** for point 4.
14. **The events file** is read incrementally by byte offset (one full read at activation) and compacted by the Cockpit above a size cap, keeping the last event per ticket. It lives in extension storage and persists across restarts, because it is a ticket's only memory of its last session id. The exact path is a spec detail.
15. **Performance bar**: VS Code's perceived responsiveness and the battery, not latency numbers. Nothing lifecycle-related on the UI path; activation renders stored state and spawns nothing until a trigger fires; every read and spawn is async in the extension host; no polling timers (every refresh has a cause: a terminal event, a status event, a registry change, window focus, the view shown); spawns debounced one second or more; the only timer is the one 15 s timeout per launch. Soft targets for the spec: a status change or an ending visible within about a second.
16. **Hidden Cockpit**: the terminal and status-event listeners stay on (they are pushed and keep the ended record right for Resume); the registry watcher stops and nothing is spawned; one refresh when the view is shown.
17. **AFK tickets launch exactly like HITL ones**; the only difference is the type icon from [How do maps render in the Cockpit?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/7).

- `claude agents --json` lists every live session (interactive and background) without a TTY: `pid, cwd, kind, startedAt, sessionId, name, status`. Measured here at 100 to 200 ms. Backed by `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, undocumented, with stale files for dead pids left behind. The docs say to read session state through the command, not the files.
- `--resume <uuid>` works from any cwd and keeps the id; `--resume <name>` resolves within the repo and its worktrees, exact match resumes, ambiguous opens the picker. A resumed worktree session returns to its worktree. `--plugin-dir`, `--mcp-config`, `--settings` and `--add-dir` are not restored on resume. `SessionStart` fires with `resume`; `--fork-session` gets `fork` and a new id. ([sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md), [worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md))
- A live interactive session started with a `-n` name another live session uses is renamed `<name>-<two words>` (2.1.232+).
- A **named** `-w` session always prompts keep-or-remove on exit, clean or not; unnamed clean ones are removed silently; no setting suppresses it. On keep, claude prints `claude --worktree <name> --resume`. A killed process leaves the worktree in place.
- Workspace trust is keyed on the repository root, so a worktree never re-triggers the dialog; `-w` in an untrusted repo exits with an error. The only non-interactive acceptance is editing `projects.<root>.hasTrustDialogAccepted` in claude's config (here `~/.claude/.claude.json`). Hooks from settings files are held back until trust is accepted. ([permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md))
- `--bg`: cannot be combined with `-p`; `-w` with `--bg` is undocumented; hooks in a background session are undocumented; a background session that edits files commits, pushes its own branch and opens a draft PR on finish, the opposite of the push-to-`main` routine; `claude rm` deletes its worktree. A window reload keeps terminal processes (`terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions`, unless `isTransient`) and rebuilds `Terminal` objects with the name but without `env`, `shellPath` or `shellArgs`; a window close kills them with `Shutdown`. No API signals that a running process waits on input. (`vscode.d.ts`, `terminalService.ts`)

Three facts for [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28): the ticket states above, the registry as a liveness source with its own `busy|idle|waiting` word, and the name match. The registry's documented `waitingFor` values (`permission prompt`, `input needed`, `dialog open`) are confirmed for background sessions only; if they fire for interactive ones, they close the dialog and Esc gaps without scraping.

`claude --bg` with `claude attach` for AFK tickets, for v0.1.0.

The **Session** term in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) and a relationship line, pushed to `main` together with the stranded [ADR 0003](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-the-cockpit-launches-and-watches.md) commit from #5. ### What was done

2. **Mocha files must be kept out of the `unit` project explicitly.** Vitest's default include is `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` from the root, which also matches the *compiled* `out-test*/**/*.test.cjs|mjs`; a Mocha file under Vitest fails on `describe` being undefined. 3. **`e2e` is opt-in by construction.** Vitest 5 has no "excluded unless named" project, so the root config lists `e2e` only when `process.argv` carries `-p`/`--project` (Vite+ loads the config in the same process, so the flag is visible). `vp test` → `unit`; `vp test --project e2e` → `e2e`; `vp test --project unit` → `unit`.

5. **Target Node 22 for the host bundles and stay CommonJS.** The floor's Node is 22.19 (the research's 20.19 was for 1.100). ESM test files are a hang on the floor, not an error, so a CI job would run to its timeout.

8. **Per-folder tsconfigs are enough.** `test/integration/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["mocha", "node", "vscode"]` and `test/e2e/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["node"]`, each `include: ["*.ts"]`; `vp check` picks them up and passes.
9. **`.vscode-test.mjs` takes an array with labels**; `vscode-test` runs every label by default and `--label floor` selects one. Glob entries work for `pack` (`test/integration/**/*.test.ts` → `out-test/extension.test.cjs`).

Which fields does the snapshot carry for each map and each ticket, and which of them are facts the tracker reports (state, parent, blockers, assignees) rather than something the scout read out of a body?

It has to fit both trackers: on GitHub a ticket is an issue with a URL and a claim is a person; on the local markdown tracker a ticket is a file path and a claim is a `Status: claimed` line that names nobody. It also has to carry drift warnings per map and per ticket, since the scout reads with code and shows anything it cannot read as drift.

## Context

- Decided in [Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/16): the scout is code only. The prototype's code reading on `prototype/scout` (`packages/core/scout-prototype/scout.mjs`, functions `parseMap`, `parseTicket`, `reconcile`) is a first draft of the fields.
- The drift catalogue: [Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/10).
- Effect Schema models the snapshot ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md)); the webview imports its types only.","labels":{"nodes":[{"name":"wayfinder:grilling"}]},"assignees":{"nodes":[{"login":"dbarjs"}]},"parent":{"number":1},"blockedBy":{"nodes":[]},"comments":{"nodes":[{"author":{"login":"dbarjs"},"createdAt":"2026-10-06T23:14:18Z","body":"## Resolution

**The snapshot is tracker-only and nested per map. It holds three kinds of value: facts the tracker reports, sections code reads from bodies, and coded drift warnings. It holds nothing derived and nothing about sessions.** Decided with Eduardo on 2026-10-06 in two grilling rounds; every recommendation stood.

### Shape

```ts
Snapshot {
  tracker: { kind: 'github', owner, repo } | { kind: 'local' }
  repoRoot: string
  collectedAt: string                 // ISO
  maps: WayfinderMap[]                // tracker order; display order is derived
  unmapped: Ticket[]                  // tickets with no map, each with a `no-map` warning
  warnings: Warning[]
}

WayfinderMap {
  number, title, ref                  // fact
  body: string                        // fact: raw Markdown, rendered by the Detail
  tickets: Ticket[]                   // fact: map order (sub-issue order / file number)
  destination: string | null          // read
  notes: string | null                // read
  decisions: { number: number | null, title: string, link: string, gist: string }[]   // read
  notYetSpecified: { text: string, tickets: number[] }[]   // read, addressed by index
  outOfScope: { text: string, tickets: number[] }[]        // read
  warnings: Warning[]
}

Ticket {
  number, title, ref                  // fact
  state: 'open' | 'closed'            // fact: issue state / `Status: resolved`
  type: 'research' | 'prototype' | 'grilling' | 'task' | null   // fact: label / `Type:` line
  claim: { by: string[] } | null      // fact: assignees / `Status: claimed` (empty `by`)
  blockedBy: Blocker[]                // fact: native dependencies / `Blocked by:` line
  body: string                        // fact: raw Markdown
  resolution: { body: string, author: string | null, at: string | null } | null   // read: last comment / `## Answer`
  outcome: 'decided' | 'out-of-scope' | 'unrecorded' | null   // read against the map; null while open
  gist: string | null                 // read: the map's Decisions-so-far line for this ticket, verbatim
  warnings: Warning[]
}

Ref     = { tracker: 'github', url: string } | { tracker: 'local', path: string }   // path is repo-relative
Blocker = { number: number, title: string, state: 'open' | 'closed', ref: Ref }
Warning = { code: WarningCode, detail?: string }
```

### Decided

1. **Identity** is a shared `number` and `title` on both trackers (the "issue numbers everywhere" rule) plus a tagged `ref` that says how to open and launch it: a URL on GitHub, a repo-relative path on a local tracker. A local ticket's `number` is its `NN` file prefix.
2. **Nested, not flat.** Tickets live under their map in map order. A ticket with no map (no native parent, no task-list entry, no `Part of` line) goes to `unmapped` with a `no-map` warning. Nothing is dropped.
3. **Facts versus reads.** Facts: number, title, ref, state, type, claim, parent and order, blockers, body. Reads: the map's five sections, the ticket's resolution, outcome and gist. The scout never guesses a read; what it cannot parse is `null` plus a warning.
4. **Provenance is a warning, not a field.** The prototype's `mapVia` and per-blocker `via` go. A value that arrived through a text fallback (`Part of #n`, a task list, `Blocked by:`) stands as a plain value with a drift warning, since v0.1.0 does not promise the fallbacks ([Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/3)).
5. **Bodies are stored raw** for both maps and tickets, because the Detail renders them as Markdown ([Where does the Cockpit live: sidebar, editor tab, or both?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/23)). Maps also carry all five sections parsed: destination and fog feed the Tree, decisions and out of scope feed the outcome, notes is cheap. Tickets carry no `question` or `summary` field; a missing `## Question` is still a warning.
6. **Resolution** is the last comment (the `## Answer` section locally), with `author` and `at` null where the tracker has none. A closed ticket with no comment gets `closed-no-resolution`.
7. **Gist** is the map's own Decisions-so-far line for the ticket, verbatim, with no computed fallback: that line was written by a human for exactly this purpose.
8. **Outcome** classifies a closed ticket by the map: listed under Decisions so far is `decided`, linked from Out of scope is `out-of-scope`, neither is `unrecorded` with a warning. GitHub's `stateReason` is ignored; the map's sections are the convention.
9. **Claim** is `{ by: string[] } | null`. Any assignee counts, matching the frontier query; `by` is empty on a local tracker, which names nobody.
10. **Blockers** are references with `number`, `title`, `state` and `ref`, so a blocker outside the map still renders in "Waits on" and still gates. `blocking` ("Clears the way for") is derived by inversion, never stored, so the two directions cannot disagree.
11. **Nothing derived.** Frontier, `next`, open-blocker counts, decided/total, the Finished fold and map ordering are pure functions exported by `@hero-synergy/core` and applied in the extension host. The snapshot is cached ([What is the scout's budget: refresh cadence, caching and rate limits?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/27)), and derived values in a cache are stale or redundant.
12. **Warnings are coded**: a closed literal union of codes with an optional free-text `detail` (which label, which line), at three levels (snapshot, map, ticket), one fixture per code. Core ships no UI copy; the Cockpit maps codes to messages. An unreadable item (a free-form map) stays in the snapshot with nulls and a warning, as [ADR 0005](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-the-scout-reads-trackers-with-code.md) asks.
13. **Timestamps**: `collectedAt` on the snapshot. Per-item `updatedAt` and local content hashes are the scout's cache keys, owned by #27, so the snapshot type does not move when the caching strategy does.
14. **The boundary**: tracker-only. Sessions, status events, worktrees and actions are joined in by the Cockpit ([How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21), [When the scout and the status hooks disagree, which does the Cockpit believe?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/28)). The "can't show maps" cases from #3 are a scout error type, not a snapshot field.
15. **HITL or AFK** is derived from `type` in the Cockpit; a task ticket shows as "task". No field, because the scout would have to guess it.
16. **Local titles** come from the file's first H1, else from the slug or the effort directory humanized, with a warning on the fallback.
17. **Names in core**: `WayfinderMap` (since `Map` shadows the global), `Ticket`, `Snapshot`, `Ref`, `Claim`, `Blocker`, `Warning`, in `packages/core/src/snapshot/`. Types exported, schema objects not ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-effect-schema-models-all-boundary-data.md)).

### Warning codes, v0.1.0

| Level | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| snapshot | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` | the repo has `wayfinder:` labels the scout does not know |
| map | `map-body-legacy` | M2, M3 or M4 headings (detail says which) |
| map | `map-body-partial` | some of the five sections, not all |
| map | `map-body-free-form` | no recognizable section |
| map | `map-no-destination` | no Destination section |
| map | `decision-line-unparsed` | a Decisions-so-far bullet is not `[title](link) — gist` |
| map | `decision-links-open-ticket` | Decisions so far links a ticket that is still open |
| map | `children-as-task-list` | children listed as a task list in the body |
| map | `map-title-from-directory` | local: no H1, title from the effort directory |
| ticket | `parent-as-part-of-line` | parent given by `Part of #n` |
| ticket | `blockers-as-text-line` | blockers given by `Blocked by:` |
| ticket | `blockers-as-slugs` | `Blocked by:` holds slugs, not numbers |
| ticket | `type-as-line` | type given by a `Type:` line on GitHub |
| ticket | `type-missing` | no type label or line |
| ticket | `type-several` | more than one type label |
| ticket | `claim-legacy-label` | `wayfinder:claimed` label |
| ticket | `unknown-wayfinder-labels` | a `wayfinder:` label the scout does not know |
| ticket | `no-question-heading` | no `## Question` |
| ticket | `closed-no-resolution` | closed with no comment or `## Answer` |
| ticket | `closed-unrecorded` | closed, in neither Decisions so far nor Out of scope |
| ticket | `no-map` | no parent found; the ticket is in `unmapped` |
| ticket | `blocker-outside-map` | a blocker that is not a ticket of the same map |
| ticket | `ticket-title-from-slug` | local: no H1, title from the file slug |
| ticket | `unknown-status` | local: a `Status:` value other than `claimed` or `resolved` |

### Not in the snapshot

Derived values; sessions, status events, worktrees and actions; per-item `updatedAt`; scout failures; provenance; raw labels; the map's body form (a warning instead); a map `state` (closed maps are never collected); a ticket `question` or `summary`; HITL/AFK.

### Local tracker

`.scratch/<effort>/map.md` is the map, `issues/NN-<slug>.md` the tickets, in number order. `state` is `Status: resolved`, `claim` is `Status: claimed`, `type` the `Type:` line, `blockedBy` the `Blocked by: NN` line, `resolution` the `## Answer` section. The effort slug a local launch command needs ([How does the Cockpit handle a session's lifecycle?](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/issues/21), point 11) is derived from the `ref` path.

### Recorded

The **Snapshot** and **Drift** terms in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/dbarjs/hero-synergy/blob/main/CONTEXT.md). No ADR: core is a private package in v0.1.0, so every field here is cheap to change.
